text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
Business:
ROMANIA LIBERA
- An offshore platform of the oil exploration company Petrom RA started drilling in the Sea of Marmara under a contract with the national oil company of Turkey.
- The leu currency depreciated a further 1.05 percent against the dollar over the last week.
ADEVARUL
- The money Romania raised on international capital markets will not be used for consumption, central bank governor Mugur Isarescu says in a front-page interview.
- Petrol prices are expected to rise more than three times in the next three or four weeks.
TINERETUL LIBER
- Romania has received no bids in its licensing round for 15 oil blocks despite a November 30 deadline.
AZI
- France Telecom plans to enter its bid for a GSM licence in Romania.
CURIERUL NATIONAL
- The private sector has seen only a modest development over the first nine months of the year.
- The recently opened over-the-counter market traded shares of only one stock -- Turbomecanica SA plane engine maker -- at its second session on Monday.
General:
ROMANIA LIBERA
- The newspaper publishes the political initiatives of Emil Constantinescu, presidential candidate of the opposition Democratic Convention (CDR), over the past seven years.

- Economic Reform Minister Mircea Cosea, parliamentary candidate of the ruling Party of Social Democracy (PDSR) in the November 3 elections, said the party was "prepared to enter opposition without any questions if it loses the polls".
- After winning the 1992 polls, President Ion Iliescu has taken some points from the opposition CDR programme but did not fulfil them, says Constantinescu in a full-page interview.
ADEVARUL
- The Hungarian parliament postponed debate on the Romanian-Hungarian friendship treaty until the end of November in order not to influence the elections in Romania.
- Miron Mitrea, vice-president of the ruling PDSR, said the party had spent 1.1 billion lei for its campaign.

- Free and fair elections are a condition for Romania to be admitted to NATO, the newspaper quotes Daniel Fried, White House adviser on Eastern Europe, who met members of the Romanian community living in the United States.
- The candidates of the Socialist Party (PS) will not disappoint their voters in the next parliament, says Tudor Mohora, head of the PS and presidential candidate.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI

- The broadcast on state television of a campaign clip with the opposition CDR presidential candidate Emil Constantinescu cut in two by a black line was not a blunder, but a deliberate attack on the candidate, says an editorial on the incident.
- Two leading producers of Romanian state television denounce "political censorship" imposed by general manager Dumitru Titus Popa.

- Adrian Paunescu, presidential candidate of the Socialist Labour Party (PSM), said he would not give his votes to any of the leading candidates - President Iliescu, Constantinescu or Former Prime Minister Petre Roman in the run-off round.
- The newspaper continues to present incidents in breach of electoral law seen by the paper as part of major fraud.
- The newspaper presents the private side of CDR candidate Constantinescu in a full-page interview.
- The campaign managers and leaders of the major parties ask that no opinion polls be presented during Sunday voting.
AZI

- "Today, here and now I hereby promise to be Romania's first social-democratic president" reads a front-page headline with excerpts of the programme of former Prime Minister Roman, running for president for the Social-Democratic Union (USD).
CRONICA ROMANA

- Adrian Nastase, executive president of the ruling PDSR and chairman of the lower Chamber of Deputies for the past four years, is most fit to be Prime Minister if the PDSR wins the November 3 polls, said PDSR vice-president Miron Mitrea.
- An Orthodox priest asks Petre Roman in an open letter to stop using the church for his electoral campaign.
ZIUA
- The Centre for political studies says in an analysis that it will be very difficult to create a stable government after the elections.
LIBRTATEA
- While President Iliescu has the support of 36 percent, 62 percent of voters are convinced that he will be re-elected, shows a survey by the Academy's sociological institute.
CURIERUL NATIONAL

- "I am running for election because the people see me as a symbol of the stability and Romania's development," says President Iliescu in a three-page interview. ($=3,367 lei) -- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
